heroHeadline: Taliban Forcibly Evicts Students From Kabul's Khatam al-Nabieen Shia Seminary, Detains 36 in Widening Crackdown
heroSubtitle: September 7, 2026 is Day 9,101 since the US launched Operation Enduring Freedom and Day 195 of Pakistan's Operation Ghazab lil-Haq. Taliban forces forcibly evicted students and teachers from Kabul's Khatam al-Nabieen Shia religious seminary and educational complex on Dar-ul-Aman Road, detaining 28 in the eviction (24 remain held) after surrounding the complex and ordering an evacuation on September 5 and detaining three prominent Shia leaders — Sufi Gardizi, Sayed Hassan Sharifi Balkhabi and Mohammad Hossein Sangardoost — on September 6, bringing the total detained across the week-long operation to roughly 36. The Taliban's Ministry of Justice claims the complex, which includes Khatam al-Nabieen University and Tamadon TV, sits on government-owned land; seminary officials dispute this and say the ownership case remains before a Taliban court. The crackdown follows a bloody stretch of Pakistani counter-insurgency operations: ISPR says security forces killed 21 Fitna al-Khawarij militants across North Waziristan, Kohat and Dera Ismail Khan between September 3-5 and revised the North Waziristan infiltration toll upward to 25, part of a 72-hour, 48-militant Balochistan sweep through September 4. No formal ceasefire or new Urumqi round has been confirmed.
